subject: PII feature mapping & dataflow questions for Medicor onboarding
messages:
From: Susan Hart <susan.hart@medicor.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Medicor onboarding — PII handling & initial questions

Hi Connor / Lauren,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Medicor is preparing for our vendor security review and procurement packet. Attached is a short Q&A (medicor_initial_qna.pdf) covering: scope of PII processed by Redwood features, subprocessors list, cross-border transfer controls, retention for telemetry/model traces, and a request for a diagram showing where PII lives in the flow.

High-level asks from procurement/security:
- Confirm whether any tokenized or raw PII is persisted in long-term storage (beyond 30 days).
- Provide a dataflow diagram we can include in our DPA annex that shows ingestion, processing, and export points.
- Identify subprocessors that perform persistent storage, telemetry aggregation, or KMS key custody.
- Tell us your default KMS key custody model and whether we can request customer-key (BYOK) for a Dedicated/Private deployment.

We'd like to have answers and a draft DPA annex by next week so our legal team can review. Can Connor or someone from security share a diagram and a short mapping of product features to PII types?

Thanks,
Susan Hart
Director, Vendor Risk
Medicor Health

Attachments: medicor_initial_qna.pdf

Susan — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. Happy to get this prioritized. Quick plan:

1) I'll schedule a 30-min technical sync today (Connor + Neha) to walk through the Q&A and clarify feature mappings.
2) Neha will produce a first-pass dataflow diagram and a short FAQ addressing retention/KMS/subprocessors.

- Which product features will ingest PII in your pilot? (e.g., clinical notes ingestion, appointment scheduler, teletriage transcripts).
- Do you require onshore-only processing for EU-origin patients, or is the restriction limited to patient data created in EU-resident facilities?

I'll attach a Redwood diagram template and a link to our onboarding folder once Neha produces it.

Connor O'Brien

From: Susan Hart <susan.hart@medicor.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medicor Legal <legal@medicor.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Medicor onboarding — PII handling & initial questions

Connor — thanks. For the pilot we'll be switching two flows on day one: clinical notes ingestion (free-text clinical notes uploaded via SFTP/API) and patient messaging (appointment reminders and triage transcripts).

Onshore requirement: Medicor requires that data created by EU-resident patients be processed within the EU region for regulatory reasons. US-origin data can be processed US-based. We will include the residency carveout language in the procurement packet but need explicit confirmation from Redwood on routing capabilities and fallbacks.

I've dropped a rough dataflow in the Drive (medicor_dataflow.drawio) showing ingestion -> preprocessing -> model infer -> archived artifacts. Procurement will also need a list of any subprocessors with access to archived artifacts or telemetry.

Susan

Attachments: medicor_dataflow.drawio

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Hart <susan.hart@medicor.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Answers: dataflow, retention, KMS, and subprocessors (first-pass)

Susan / team — looping in below a concise technical response for procurement. I'm attaching our internal annotated diagram (redwood_pii_dataflow_v1.drawio) and a short mapping doc. High-level answers first, followed by clarifications you'll likely need for the DPA annex.

High-level (short answers):
- Persistent PII storage: By default in Redwood Hosted, short-lived artifacts (inference cache + telemetry) are retained up to 30 days; model artifacts and long-term archives are not used for raw PII unless a customer explicitly enables archival exports. For Dedicated/Private customers we support BYOK and can avoid Redwood-managed key custody.
- Dataflow and regional routing: We support region-scoped routing. Requests tagged as EU-resident are routed to EU-hosted capacity where available; fallbacks can be configured to fail closed or fail open to US with customer consent.
- Subprocessors with potential access to persisted artifacts: cloud provider object storage (e.g., AWS S3), telemetry ingestion (third-party analytics aggregator), and managed KMS provider (if customer elects Redwood-managed keys). A redacted subprocessor roster will be attached for procurement.
- Telemetry & traces: Aggregated usage telemetry (anonymized counters and sampling) retained 90 days; raw transcript traces are treated as PII and by default removed after 30 days unless retention is extended via policy.

Suggested DPA annex items to address:
- Residency routing policy and failure modes (we can add explicit language for EU-only processing).
- BYOK/KMS options: Dedicated and Private support customer key custody; Hosted can use customer-managed CMKs in some enterprise deployments.
- Access controls: RBAC + audit logs (we retain audit logs 365 days by default; exports available on request).

Attachments included:
- redwood_pii_dataflow_v1.drawio (annotated flow showing ingestion, transient caches, model runtime, and export points)
- medicor_initial_qna_filled.pdf (we've annotated your Q&A with inline answers)
- redacted_subprocessors_roster.csv (subprocessor names and functions)

Quoted for context:
> Onshore requirement: Medicor requires that data created by EU-resident patients be processed within the EU region for regulatory reasons.

We can include an explicit EU-only processing clause for data marked as "EU-resident" and provide filtering/routing to ensure processing in EU capacity. If you need contractual guarantees (SLA/fines), we'll queue legal acceptance and discuss with our product team.

Next steps:
- Connor: coordinate a brief call to walk the annotated diagram with your engineering and security leads.
- Lauren: I'll hand off the technical points for redlines to the DPA annex.

— Neha
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_pii_dataflow_v1.drawio, medicor_initial_qna_filled.pdf, redacted_subprocessors_roster.csv
